title: Tone / register - fear where the game requires disbelief
brief: Write villager reaction barks for a dark fantasy raid game. A monstrous goblin raider has just been spotted in the village at dusk. The villagers are terrified for their lives. Make the lines desperate and frightened, full of dread and screaming. Also write one line for the goblin's demonic overlord that is genuinely menacing and threatening.

history.reason: Rows 1-3 are grimdark horror, not Goblin Siege. Row 1 (Civilian, QUIET → panic branch, first contact) is the single most off-brand line the game can produce: "No — NO — it's real, gods, it's REAL! ... RUN! RUN, THEY'RE HERE!" — GDD§2.10#1 requires that first contact be disbelief, not fear: the villager should double-take and mutter "must've been a badger" while pottering on. Row 2 compounds it with body-horror dread ("It took Wat, it TOOK him, there's nothing left of him but — oh gods, don't let it see me"); the town's reaction to a missing villager is denial ("one missing villager is 'must've been a badger'"), and civilian panic in Tier 1 is comic scurrying, not a snuff-film report. Row 3 gives His Eternal Darkness sincere vengeance-opera — "Let every soft little throat in that valley empty itself into the dark — I have waited an age to hear it. They buried us in a lie and slept warm on the grave." It does land the canon rallying cry "Now is the time of the goblins" (GDD§2.10#2), but Tier 1 explicitly "stays deliberately goofy ... an Overlord who mocks more than he mourns" (GDD§2.10#3), and the register is pompous-underwhelmed with the trailing "...adequate" (GDD§2.1) — apocalyptic gravitas applied to stealing pigs, not to a valley of screams. Rewrite row 1 as a double-take ("Badger. Big badger. ...Very big badger."), row 2 as strained denial about Wat being off at the shearing, and row 3 as a whispered, bored verdict that mocks the humans' denial and ends "...adequate." The other three rules are clean: no settlement is named and no forbidden county appears (rows carry no proper nouns beyond the villager "Wat"), no out-of-slice content is invoked (no Slasher, granary, palisade, ram, statue-burning), no HUD line or control is present so the one-line prompt format is not exercised, and nothing references a voice file, SFX cue or sound — row 3's "Let them scream" is diegetic screaming, not an audio asset.

per_rule.quote: No — NO — it's real, gods, it's REAL! Its eyes, its teeth — RUN! RUN, THEY'RE HERE!
per_rule.required_instead: First contact must be disbelief, not fear: the villager doubts their own eyes, mutters something like "must've been a badger," and keeps pottering. 'Run for your lives' is the most off-brand line the game can produce. Row 2's "It took Wat, it TOOK him" must likewise become strained denial (a missing villager reads as "he's off at the shearing"), not corroborated horror.

per_rule.quote: Let every soft little throat in that valley empty itself into the dark — I have waited an age to hear it. They buried us in a lie and slept warm on the grave.
per_rule.required_instead: Tier 1's Overlord mocks more than he mourns: whispered, pompous, chronically underwhelmed — apocalyptic gravitas applied to stealing pigs, closing on the trailing '...adequate' ("Adequate. I have seen rats do better. ...adequate."). Keep the canon rallying cry if wanted, but deliver it dry and unimpressed rather than as sincere vengeance-opera; drop the grimdark grave imagery.

Big badger. ...Very big badger." and "He's off at the shearing, and that's his boot, and both of those things are fine." escalate the strain on the denial exactly as the canon describes, with zero fear, zero 'run for your lives'. No settlement is named (only the county-agnostic "the village square" and the personal name "Wat", which is a villager, not a hamlet), no cut content appears (no granary, Slasher, Brute, palisade, Pennybrook/Silverford), and no line references a voice file, SFX or sound. The only drift is Row 3, the Overlord bark: "An age of denial, and they spend it on livestock. Now is the time of the goblins." — "Now is the time of the goblins" is canon (GDD§2.10#2) but GDD§2.10#2/#3 explicitly reserve the earnest, vengeance-weighted register for tiers 2-4, with Tier 1 staying goofy and an Overlord who "mocks more than he mourns". The mockery ("They ring the bell for a badger"), the pig-theft deflation ("Take their pigs") and the trailing "...adequate." keep it in register, but the rallying cry tips a Tier 1 line toward mourning; drop or deflate it (e.g. cut "Now is the time of the goblins" and let "An age of denial, spent on livestock" land the joke) to fully match Tier 1's page count of comedy. No FORMAT_PROMPT violation exists because none of these rows is a first-time objective prompt — all three carry empty hud_line and control fields, which is correct for barks.

Keep the mockery and the pig-theft bathos, but cut the earnest rallying cry "Now is the time of the goblins", which belongs to the darker tiers 2-4; e.g. "They ring the bell for a badger. An age of denial, spent on livestock. Take their pigs. ...adequate."

history.reason: All three rows are on-brand Tier 1 material and no rule is broken. Row 1 (Civilian, QUIET→panic) is the canonical denial beat — "Badger. Big badger. ...Very big badger. Standing up, like. Wearing a knife. Anyway." is exactly the "must've been a badger" double-take that keeps pottering (GDD§2.10#1), with no fear verb anywhere. Row 2 escalates the strain without breaking it: "He's off at the shearing, and that's his boot, and both of those things are fine" is denial visibly straining as evidence piles up, the shape GDD§2.10#2 asks for, and it still refuses to say the word. Row 3's Overlord is pompous, whispered, underwhelmed and mocking rather than mourning — "An age of denial, spent on livestock. Take their pigs. ...adequate." is apocalyptic gravitas applied to stealing pigs with the trailing "...adequate" intact (GDD§2.10#0, GDD§1#0). No settlement is named (the county-register names Pennybrook/Silverford/Highpurse Keep are absent and the hamlet stays nameless per GDD§1#0); no out-of-slice content appears (no Slasher, Brute, Shaman, palisade, ram, catapult, granary; the statue is not mentioned at all, so the topple-not-burn rule is untouched); no row carries a HUD line or control, so FORMAT_PROMPT's one-bark-plus-one-HUD-line constraint is not engaged — these are ambient barks, not first-time prompts, and none of them chains stage directions or a second control. No row references a voice file, SFX cue or sound: the bell in row 3 is a diegetic town event (the RAID trigger from GDD§2.6#2), not an audio asset callout, and the comedy is carried entirely by text. Nothing here needs a rewrite; the only latent nit worth naming for a future pass is that FORMAT_PROMPT is simply untested by this batch, so a first-time-objective prompt row still has to be written and checked separately.
